name: Llyr

attributes.attribute: the same as the Irish Lir to some

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Llyr, or Lear, is a Welsh god of whom little is known. Some set him as the same as the Irish sea god LIR. Others read him as a god of the OTHERWORLD. The Celts also told that otherworld as an island in the sea or as land under the waves, so the two views fit well. Llyr was father of the hero MANAWYDAN. In later lore he became the king known as Llyr Llediath, the Llyr of the foreign accent, and a saint said to rest under the River Saahr. Geoffrey of Monmouth tells of a King Leir from whom William Shakespeare drew his mad king Lear.

okr.objective: Set the Welsh god Llyr and his later king form.
key_results: Give the two readings of the god.
Note his saint form and the Lear link to Shakespeare.
